transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM), Maya (Aurora VP Eng), Derek (Aurora SRE), Nina (Aurora Security), Omar (Aurora Infra), Priya (Aurora Product)

Summary: quick follow up to the Jan-12 incident where we saw elevated tail latency and a small percentage of request failures when traffic spiked after a batch import. Focus: root cause confirmation, short-term mitigations, and medium-term reliability improvements.

Topics: postmortem findings, KV cache corruption hypothesis, fallback routing, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, audit logs and KMS, next steps and SLAs

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: okay hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um let's do a quick roll call, and then we'll go through the postmortem items. Maya?
00:07 Maya: hi yes Maya here, and we have Derek, Nina, Omar and Priya on from the Aurora side.
00:12 Samir: awesome thanks. Leah, do you want to run the incident summary briefly?
00:17 Leah: yeah sure. so quick recap, on 2027-01-12 at around 02:40 UTC Aurora hit a traffic spike from the nightly import job then we saw a 0.8% increase in 5xx errors and tail latency jump to 4.2s at P99 for text generation routes, so, um, root causes we identified were a KV cache invalidation race combined with a fallback cascade to a heavier model variant which saturated a small pool of dedicated instances.
00:43 Derek: to be clear the app was doing repeated retries which amplified the load, right, that's what we saw on our side?
00:48 Leah: yeah there were retries and then the traffic hit the fallback path which picked the, uh, larger model because the smaller quantized variant had an unresolved cache miss, so you get hot shards on the larger model.
00:58 Nina: quick question, do we know if any keys were leaked or if it's just cache inconsistency? security is mostly concerned about data leakage.
01:04 Leah: initial analysis shows inconsistent KV state only, not data exfiltration. there was no exposure of the request payloads outside of the cluster. we did see incomplete cache writes during the window; the writes were retried but the race left some entries stale.
01:16 Maya: ok that's good, we needed confirmation on that.
01:18 Samir: thanks. Carlos, you had the mitigation timeline earlier?
01:21 Carlos: yes. short term we did three things: paused the nightly import to prevent repeat spike, increased capacity on the dedicated fallback pool, and pushed a hotfix to make the fallback selection rate-limited. medium term Leah's team will run the KV-cache repro and we will implement stronger cache write durability and a read-through fallback that doesn't cascade immediately. long term is a routing policy change and automatic shedding to protect P99.
01:44 Omar: what do you mean by "read-through fallback that doesn't cascade immediately" — can you explain?
01:49 Leah: sure, right now when a cache miss occurs the system may route to a larger model and also trigger pre-warm calls which in our case overlapped and compounded — the idea is to make the first fallback return a lightweight degraded response or a queued pre-warm rather than routing N requests to the heavy model immediately. it's a graceful degrade.
02:09 Priya: what's the impact on latency for the consumer, like will they see more timeouts versus slower responses?
02:13 Leah: they'll see a controlled degrade, usually a slightly higher 95 but lower P99 spikes because we avoid saturating the heavy model.
02:19 Derek: on our infra side we recorded a burst of queue depth which caused backpressure into the retriers in the app, so yeah the cascade made it worse.
02:28 Samir: ok let's dig into the repro, Leah can you describe the steps you need from Aurora?
02:33 Leah: we need the sample request IDs and the payloads for the window 02:35-03:05 UTC on Jan 12; also the runbook that kicked off the import job and any retry settings in the app. if you can provide those Derek that will let us run the targeted KV cache repro on our dedicated staging cluster.
02:50 Derek: I can get the IDs and the payloads, there might be PII redaction needed, we'll coordinate with Nina.
02:56 Nina: yes we'll scrub PHI and share a sanitized set, we just need to confirm the expected redaction policy with Redwood, is there a standard template?
03:03 Samir: we have a sanitized payload template, I'll send it after the call.
03:07 Maya: on the SLAs, our execs want a timeline for preventing recurrence and for the capacity/compensating controls — what can you commit?
03:14 Samir: short-term remediation we've already implemented: rate-limited fallback, extra capacity, and paused import. we'll deliver a written postmortem with a remediation timeline by Friday 2027-01-22. medium-term changes like read-through fallback and cache write durability plan will be in the 4-6 week road map. long-term routing policy and autoshed changes will be discussed for Q2 planning.
03:34 Priya: do you have a cost impact estimate for the extra capacity? CFO asked about potential monthly spend increase if we keep higher capacity.
03:40 Carlos: preliminary estimate is around 8-12% uplift in monthly dedicated costs if Aurora keeps the expanded pool; we can provide a detailed cost model after we repro and size the fix.
03:50 Maya: are there data residency or KMS implications from the logs and debug captures you need? security would like to ensure audit logs stay in-region and keys are customer-managed.
03:58 Samir: yes we can support KMS/HSM per the Private deployment model; for this debug capture we can store logs in Aurora's S3 and we will not bring them into Redwood's hosted buckets. Nina, can you confirm the KMS key ARN you want us to use for encrypted upload?
04:12 Nina: we'll provide a KMS key and a target bucket — we'll share the details by 2027-01-26.
04:18 Leah: one more thing on reproducibility — the race seems to trigger when concurrent imports coincide with a cold-start pattern on quantized models. we suspect a window where the write-back path uses a non-atomic sequence; our fix is to make the write atomic and add a small TTL jitter to avoid thundering herd.
04:36 Derek: that aligns with our logs, we saw write attempts overlapping. can you make the write idempotent too?
04:41 Leah: yes idempotency is part of the fix.
04:44 Maya: will this require downtime or a canary? we can't have full downtime.
04:48 Samir: no downtime; we plan a rolling canary on dedicated staging first, then gradual rollout with canary traffic on production. we'll coordinate maintenance windows if needed but we don't expect full service interruption.
05:00 Omar: what about monitoring — can you add alerting for cache-write-failure rate and for fallback-induced model saturation?
05:06 Carlos: yes, we already added a temp alert; long-term we'll add more signals into the Redwood Console for per-route P99 tracking and automatic fallback thresholds.
05:16 Priya: from product POV we need a clear UX for degraded responses — is there an agreed taxonomy for degraded vs error vs retry?
05:22 Leah: currently we return a 200 with a small notice in the metadata when we can serve a degraded answer; otherwise we still return error codes. we can work with Aurora on the exact contract.
05:31 Nina: also security wants confirmation about audit logs for those degraded responses and whether they include any sensitive fields.
05:36 Samir: audit logs will include request IDs and metadata only, payloads will be redacted unless Aurora explicitly authorizes transfer for repro.
05:44 Derek: small nit — there are references in the initial postmortem to "K V cache corruption" spelled as KV, sometimes K-V in the logs, just be consistent.
05:51 Leah: noted, we'll normalize terminology.
05:54 Maya: can you walk quickly through the specific mitigations and who owns them?
05:59 Samir: sure, short term: pause import (Aurora owner), added pool capacity (Redwood ops), rate-limited fallback (Redwood SE). medium term: atomic cache writes + TTL jitter + idempotency (Redwood SE), read-through graceful fallback (Redwood product & SE), improved monitoring & alerts (Redwood ops + Aurora). long term: routing policy changes & autoshed (product + infra).
06:21 Priya: timeline check — when will you have the repro results?
06:24 Leah: if we get the payloads and IDs by Jan 24 we should have repro and a draft fix by Jan 27.
06:30 Maya: good. execs will want a short slide deck summarizing root cause, fix, and risk reduction. can you do that?
06:36 Carlos: yes we'll prepare an exec one-pager as part of the postmortem deliverable.
06:40 Nina: on the legal/compliance side we might need a copy of the audit logs for our auditors; what's the retention policy?
06:45 Samir: default retention is 90 days for debug logs, but we can arrange extended retention or export if needed as an add-on.
06:53 Derek: do you have any sense of whether Dedicated vs Private would change this failure mode? like if we were on Private with customer-controlled KMS and VPC does the same KV race still possible?
06:59 Leah: the race is at the application-level KV semantics, it's model/runtime agnostic; Private deployment reduces surface around network/different tenancy but won't magically remove application races. the fix is code-level atomicity. that said, Private does give you more control over capacity and routing policies which helps mitigation.
07:18 Maya: any competitor mentions in our prep doc — there was a note about other vendors doing different fallback strategies, can you share the comparison?
07:24 Samir: yeah we compared to Mistral-managed services and in-house approaches; some vendors avoid fallback and just throttle which shifts failure to client; we prefer graceful degrade + routing policy. we'll include a short appendix.
07:36 Priya: final check on cost — if we do the read-through fallback will it increase egress or compute?
07:41 Leah: read-through adds slightly more compute in the lite path but saves cost by preventing heavy model saturation; overall expected to reduce P99 cost over time. we'll provide numbers after repro.
07:54 Maya: ok I'm comfortable with the plan, as long as we get the postmortem and the exec slide deck.
07:59 Samir: great, quick recap of next steps — Leah runs repro after Aurora shares payloads (Derek) and Leah shares logs; Samir shares sanitized payload template; Carlos will prepare the exec deck; Nina shares KMS details. everyone agree?
08:16 Maya: yes
08:17 Derek: yes
08:18 Nina: yes
08:19 Samir: perfect, we'll follow up in email and lock the exec time. thanks everyone.

References/shared artifacts: postmortem-draft.docx (link), exec-onepager.pptx (link), repro-instructions.md (link to internal playbook).

End of transcript.
